outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Minor paraphrasing/extra elaboration in the objective (e.g., adding “test NASA’s human deep space capabilities”) is acceptable as long as it aligns with NASA’s described purpose. Formatting/bullets are also irrelevant.

Critical issues: The key potential failure is whether Artemis II was correctly identified as the “next planned” Artemis mission. In the final DOM state (NASA’s Artemis II mission page), the page includes an explicit status-like label “Occurred 6 months ago,” which directly conflicts with interpreting Artemis II as an upcoming/next planned mission. While the same page also shows a (future) launch date/year (“LaunchED: April 1, 2026”) and mission type (“Crewed Lunar Flyby”), that inconsistency means the agent did not reliably establish, from NASA’s own content, that Artemis II is the next planned mission. The agent also did not acknowledge or resolve this contradiction by checking another NASA scheduling/mission-order source page.

What the agent did achieve: It did use NASA.gov as the source of truth and correctly extracted the requested fields (name, year, destination framing, objective-style summary) from the Artemis II mission page content. However, because the task’s central requirement is specifically to find the NEXT planned Artemis mission, and the available NASA DOM evidence the agent relied on contains explicit text suggesting Artemis II already occurred, an average user would not be confident that the agent identified the correct “next planned” mission. This undermines the primary deliverable even though the extracted Artemis II details themselves are well-supported by the page.
outcome.primary_intent: Identify the next upcoming/planned Artemis mission using NASA.gov as the authoritative source, and report four specific fields: mission name, planned launch year, destination, and the mission’s primary objective. A reasonable user would be flexible on phrasing/paraphrase of destination/objective, but not flexible on picking the wrong “next planned” mission or reporting details not supported by NASA pages.

arguments.thoughts: Go directly to NASA’s Artemis section from the homepage to find the next planned Artemis mission and its details.
Artemis II is likely the next planned mission after Artemis I; opening its dedicated page should give specific launch year, destination, and objective details.
